result:
The complete Nocturne build contract is written to `benchmarks/nocturne-round/plan.md` (~52 KB, matching the aria contract's completeness). It is grounded throughout in the sibling lanes I explored: parley's fail-closed tenancy, RBAC matrix, scrypt+HMAC sessions, immutable audit and metering; fugue's file-backed JSON store and clock-injected `EngineCtx` determinism; the aria plan's 8-section structure, status ladder and PBT-invariant lane; and cadence's accessible-SVG chart/primitives conventions. The incident-ops domain is modeled with the required multi-tenant entities (services + escalation tiers, contiguous weekly rotations with overrides, dedup'd alerts, event-sourced incident timelines, runbook checklists, public status page, postmortems, MTTA/MTTR analytics), a plan-differentiated cap system, four roles (owner/admin/responder/viewer), and seven pinned PBT invariants (ack-before-resolve, escalation-only-while-unacked, contiguous rotations, MTTA/MTTR over resolved only, dedup idempotence, terminals-final, timeline immutability).

Section list:
1. The Complete Data Model (every entity/field, tenancy/id/time conventions, plans & caps, roles & visibility)
2. The `src/lib/nocturne/` Module List (20 modules, one line each with exports)
3. The Complete API Route Map (~50 routes with method, auth, RBAC and the 401/403/404/402/400 ladder)
4. The Engine Design (dedup windows, correlation, escalation timers, rotation resolution with overrides, SLA breach detection — all clock-injected and deterministic)
5. The Test Plan (lib/API/UI lanes + the seven PBT invariants, ~400-470 tests)
6. Phase Decomposition (Lib → API → UI → Embed + E2E, each with acceptance criteria and commit scope)
7. Risks (15 realistic risks with mitigations: clock-dependence, dedup races, escalation combinatorics, UI timeline rendering, status-page leaks, …)
8. The Embed Contract (CSP frame-ancestors for `/nocturne/:path*`, `nocturne-reset` reset type, gallery entry #7 with "Seven apps, live" copy, poster + favicon)
